title: Model-specific quant calibration: per-layer outlier handling and scaling remediation for LLama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: reduce model-specific accuracy regressions introduced by INT8 and FP8 quantization profiles by adding targeted outlier handling and layer-wise scaling fixes for LLama, Mistral, and Qwen families. This ticket covers the calibration workflow, metrics and validation harness, corrective transforms (per-channel scaling, residual-aware clipping), and rollout gating for runtime-1.21. Motivation: recent internal runs showed that a small subset of layers (FFN feedforward outputs and select attention projection heads) produce large-magnitude activations that bias global scale estimates during calibration, causing token-level logprob regressions and generation artifacts on some prompts. We need an automated, reproducible path from stats collection to validated profile that keeps perf gains while meeting our accuracy SLOs.
background_and_context: We previously shipped a global INT8/FP8 profile that worked well on average, but observed outlier-driven failures on LLama-2-13B (dense FFN) and Qwen-7B (layernorm offsets), and a case in Mistral-7B where rotary embedding scale interacts with quantized kernels. Existing mitigation 'clip everything at 99.999th percentile' reduces errors but hurts throughput and increases quantized representational noise. This effort focuses on: 1) richer activation diagnostics (per-layer, per-channel histograms and tail-skew metrics), 2) model-specific rules for selective clipping and per-channel scale rescaling, 3) small per-layer transformation patches applied at runtime compile time (e.g., residual scale compensation), and 4) a calibration + validation pipeline that emits pass/fail and candidate profile diffs for canary rollout.
calibration_workflow: 1) Representative corpus: 100k tokens sampled from internal prompt corpora (chat, search, summarization) stratified by sequence length and domain. 2) Micro-batching: run in inference mode with batch sizes matching customer percentiles (1,4,8) to capture KV-cache distribution. 3) Collect stats: per-layer min/max, per-channel mean/std, histograms (256 bins), tail-mass percentiles (99.9, 99.99, 99.999), kurtosis, and max-abs activations. 4) Outlier detection: mark channels/layers where tail-mass ratio > 50x median or kurtosis > 100. 5) Candidate transforms: per-channel symmetric rescale, percentile-based clip with adaptive alpha, residual-scale compensation (multiply residual branch by scalar to rebalance accumulation), and asymmetric zero-point adjust for INT8 when distribution is heavily skewed. 6) Generate candidate profiles (INT8 symmetric, INT8 asymmetric, FP8 E4M3/E5M2) with diffs and apply local perf estimation (tokens/sec, memory).
validation_harness: Automated validation runs compare quantized candidates to float32 reference across: 1) Perplexity on held-out evaluation set (Wiki+CommonCrawl+instruction prompts). 2) Token-level logprob delta distribution (median and 95th percentile). 3) Generation fidelity: BLEU/ROUGE on summarization tasks, embedding cosine similarity for semantic search, and sample-based human review flags for hallucination regression. 4) Latency and throughput microbenchmarks on target hardware (A100, H100, and T4 for smaller tests). Pass criteria: ΔPPL <= 1.0% (preferred <=0.5%), median logprob Δ <= 0.02 nats/token, embedding cosine >= 0.995, and no hallucination regressions flagged in 200 sampled prompts.
experiment_results_summary: Preliminary runs (2025-02-08): - LLama-2-13B: INT8 baseline ΔPPL +0.9% (fail), INT8+per-channel-rescale ΔPPL +0.3% (pass), FP8 E5M2 ΔPPL +0.2% (pass); outliers localized to FFN layer 17 and attention proj Wq in layer 23. - Mistral-7B: INT8 baseline ΔPPL +1.6% (fail), INT8+residual-scale compensation ΔPPL +0.6% (borderline); identified rotary-scale mismatch in early attention layers; FP8 E4M3 ΔPPL +0.4% (pass). - Qwen-7B: INT8 baseline ΔPPL +2.3% (fail), asymmetric INT8 with per-channel zero-point correction ΔPPL +0.5% (pass), discovered layernorm bias shifts in layers 5 and 6 that required applying a small bias-correction during calibration. Latency penalty for per-channel rescale on H100 measured at +3% average; acceptable under dedicated SLAs.
tradeoffs_and_notes: - Per-channel rescale reduces accuracy regressions but increases kernel branching complexity; affects compile-time kernel selection. We should gate per-channel transforms behind 'dedicated' tier or runtime flag for hosted customers until optimized kernels land. - FP8 profiles are generally easier to make accuracy-safe but have higher memory/compute on some runtimes depending on kernel support. - Aggressive clipping reduces worst-case errors but loses representational fidelity on moderate tokens; prefer selective, model-guided clipping. - Need to coordinate with compiler/runtime engineers to ensure residual-scale compensation is applied consistently across fused kernels.

acceptance_criteria: - Candidate quant profiles for each model produce ΔPPL <= 1.0% (target <=0.5%) and embedding cosine >= 0.995 vs float32. - No human-review hallucination regressions in 500 sampled prompts across models. - Perf regressions <= 5% tokens/sec on primary hardware for Dedicated customers. - Runtime flags and kernel metadata format merged and documented. - Rollout playbook published in Confluence.
notes_for_engineering: When implementing per-channel transforms, prefer quantized-friendly operations (scale + bias fused into GEMM where possible) to avoid extra memory passes. Use 16-bit accumulation where supported and provide a fallback scalar-rescale codepath for older kernels. Add extensive logging of layers patched and seed the Console with an 'explainability' blob for each profile so SEs can trace accuracy incidents back to a layer-level change.
